entries.test: Public productivity studies and national economic data available by publication would establish whether ChatGPT or generative AI had produced tenfold employee productivity gains or radical GDP increases at scale.
entries.note: The introduction attributes following material to Laura Bratton, and the supplied text does not clearly mark where that attribution ends. Marcus nevertheless presents the assertion approvingly.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and studies of realized generative AI returns, compared with documented investment totals through publication, would test whether documentable returns remained minimal against trillions invested.
entries.note: Attribution remains ambiguous following the Bratton introduction. The proposition extracts the factual premise rather than the accompanying judgment that it is perverse.

entries.test: Public bankruptcy court records would establish whether Character.AI had filed for bankruptcy by October 14, 2026.
entries.note: The postscript asserts this directly in Marcus's voice.

entries.test: Public CoreWeave bond quotations through October 14, 2026 would establish whether yields reached 15%, while credit spreads and financing terms would test the asserted deterioration in lending appetite.
entries.note: The proposition adds a sector-wide reference to AI infrastructure lending that Marcus does not specify. The yield assertion is directly testable; 'had enough' is an interpretive gloss.
